mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in TRANSIT mobility (rising from -46.4 to -41.9 over four weeks) signals restoration of commuting infrastructure and public confidence. This enables retail foot traffic recovery as workers resume office presence and pass through retail zones during transit.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT continuing its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (12.0% above baseline) combined with declining PARKS usage (-65.4%) indicates consumers are substituting outdoor recreation with indoor retail-and-recreation activities. This substitution effect drives RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -60 percent while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 percent
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -50 percent without corresponding increase in RETAIL_REC, or RESIDENTIAL drops below 8 percent.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -36 percent over four weeks with minimal week-on-week volatility. This stability signals that workplace capacity restrictions are fixed and predictable, allowing retail operators to staff and stock inventory confidently, supporting retail recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES variance across four weeks is less than 2 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range -38.6 to -36.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES volatility exceeds 3 percentage points week-on-week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite workplace stability.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable at approximately -18 percent, indicating consistent essential-goods purchasing. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the first week following this snapshot despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining within -17 to -19 range.

RETAIL_REC at -43 percent (least depressed of the four weeks) suggests seasonal demand is beginning to emerge. This seasonal lift will continue over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher.

evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -46.3 to -43.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 28 days despite historical seasonal patterns favoring September-October retail activity.

If TRANSIT begins accelerating (crossing -35 percent threshold), it signals policy relaxation, triggering return-to-office behavior that will drive RETAIL_REC recovery within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves above -35 percent while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 percent
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -35 percent but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the following two weeks, or RESIDENTIAL drops below 10 percent before TRANSIT threshold is reached.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely depressed (-65.4%), indicating outdoor recreation is constrained or avoided. candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -60 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -65.4 in most recent week, -67.1 prior week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains below -60 percent but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, or PARKS recovers above -50 percent without prior RETAIL_REC gains.
